o: What is left of a living thing from long ago, like a bone, shell, leaf, or footprint
A rock that wind carved into the shape of an animal
A plant or animal that is still alive today
A crystal that grows deep underground

q.q: A fish dies and sinks to the bottom of a lake. What has to happen next for it to become a fossil?
o: Wind and rain wear the rock away.
The fish floats back to the top.
Mud covers it, layer after layer.
A scientist digs it up right away.

q.q: A scientist finds a fossil coral in a dry desert. What does this evidence most likely tell us?
o: The place has always been a dry desert.
The wind blew the coral there from far away.
Coral lives in deserts today.
The desert was once covered by a warm, shallow ocean.

q.q: A fossil tooth is wide and flat with bumps on top. What did the animal most likely eat?
o: Rocks and sand
Plants
Other animals
Nothing at all

q.q: In rock layers that nothing has flipped or mixed, the deeper layers are older than the layers above them.
Which sentence is an observation, not an inference?
o: The fossil footprint has three toes.
A dinosaur walked here long ago.
The animal that made it was a fast runner.
This place was once a swamp.

q.q: Which is the strongest scientific inference about a tooth fossil?
o: I think this animal ate plants.
This animal likely ate plants because its teeth are flat and wide.
This animal looked weird.
This is a really cool fossil.

q.q: A scientist finds a fossil in dark, fine-grained mudstone. What does the kind of rock add to her investigation?
o: Nothing. Only the fossil matters.
It tells her the exact age of the fossil.
It proves the animal lived in a desert.
It is more data. Dark mudstone forms in wet places like swamps.

q.q: Dinosaur footprints are found in mudstone. What do the footprints tell us about that ground long ago?
o: It was covered in ice.
It was the bottom of a deep ocean.
It was soft, wet mud.
It was hard, dry rock.

q.q: Which of these can become fossils? Choose ALL that are correct.
o: Shells
Footprints
A pebble that was never alive
Bones
